relations.note: They appear as companions and fellow members of the later heroic trio.
Alyosha falsely reports Dobrynya dead and attempts to marry his wife.
Alyosha falsely reports Dobrynya dead and seeks to marry Nastasia.
The disguised Dobrynya returns, exposes Alyosha, and humiliates or beats him.
After exposing Alyosha, Dobrynya beats or threatens him in some versions.
Dobrynya is explicitly Alyosha’s sworn brother in failed-marriage songs.
Alyosha campaigns beside Ilya in later ensemble tales and composite songs.
relations.source: Tale of the Seven Russian Bogatyrs

relations.note: Alyosha appears as Ilya's junior comrade in collective heroic episodes.
Some variants make Alyosha a rival or provocative junior hero.
Alyosha appears with Ilya as the youngest member of the conventional triad.
Their contest ends in alliance and named or cross-brotherhood.

relations.myth: Defense of Kyiv and the heroic outpost
relations.note: Dobrynya is Ilya's comrade, messenger, and fellow defender in several songs.
They initially fight after failing to recognize or acknowledge each other.
Dobrynya persuades the estranged Ilya to return to Vladimir’s feast.
He is a possible father-in-law, inferred from Nastasia’s patronymic.
Ilya witnesses or buries Svyatogor, then speaks with Mikula.
The heroes become sworn companions after their unequal encounter.

relations.myth: Sworn brotherhood in the Holy Mountains
relations.note: Svyatogor accepts Ilya as his younger sworn brother and traveling companion.
Ilya tests himself against the giant and proves substantially weaker.
Ilya strikes Svyatogor, who pockets Ilya and his horse.
relations.source: Rybnikov and Hilferding northern field records

relations.note: Dying Svyatogor transfers strength and sometimes his sword to Ilya.

relations.myth: Transfer of strength from the destined coffin
relations.note: Svyatogor transmits part of his strength to Ilya by breath, foam, sweat, or vapor.
Svyatogor enables Ilya to wield or inherit his sword or weapon.
The aged Svyatogor entrusts his sword to Ilya before becoming a mountain.
Svyatogor captains the Falcon Ship while Ilya serves as his esaul.
relations.source: Ilya Muromets with Svyatogor on the Falcon Ship

relations.note: The 1956 film gives Ilya a wife named Vasilisa.
Marya joins Ivan’s repeated attempts to escape from Koschei.
Ivan marries the warrior queen Marya Morevna.
Marya receives Ivan, falls in love with him, and marries him.
Marya steals Koschei’s handkerchief and supplies it to Ivan.
Ivan repeatedly attempts to recover Marya after releasing her captive Koschei.
Ivan returns with the superior horse, kills Koschei, and frees Marya.
Ivan marries the enchanted frog, later standardized as Vasilisa.
Ivan prematurely burns her frog skin, causing her departure and his quest.
Ivan journeys to a distant realm to recover his enchanted wife.
Svyatogor cannot lift Mikula’s earth-weight bag, which Mikula handles easily.

relations.myth: The bag containing the earth's weight
relations.note: Mikula easily carries the bag that Svyatogor cannot lift.
Mikula directs Svyatogor to the supernatural smith who foretells his marriage.
After the unequal contest, Vol’ga and Mikula become companions or administrative partners.
Mikula’s strength, plow, and mare surpass Vol’ga and his entire force.

god_relations.note: Alyosha appeals to Perun in Radishchev’s modern literary reconstruction.

god_relations.myth: Establishment of Perun’s idol at Novgorod
god_relations.note: The historical Dobrynya establishes Perun’s idol above the Volkhov.
Ivan obtains and crushes the egg containing Koschei's external life.
Baba Yaga tests, feeds, directs, or equips Ivan during several quests.
Ivan gives the imprisoned Koschei water, restoring his supernatural strength.
Koschei kills, dismembers, barrels, and casts away Ivan after repeated escapes.
Ivan kills Koschei in combat, then burns and disperses his remains.
Ivan destroys Koschei's external life with the Firebird's assistance.
Cosmas rhetorically calls Libuše and her sisters three Eumenides.
Marya captures Koschei and keeps him suspended on twelve chains.
After escaping his chains, Koschei abducts and forcibly confines Marya.
Marya questions Koschei, learns his horse’s origin, and secretly informs Ivan.
Valente deliberately reimagines Marya as Koschei’s bride and principal consciousness.
Vasilisa performs household labor and grain-sorting to obtain fire.
Baba Yaga gives Vasilisa a glowing skull after she passes the tests.
Mythological reconstruction identifies Volkh’s serpent father as Veles in serpent form.

Alexander the Great.note: Modern scholarship proposes Alexander as a contributor to Marko’s conqueror and giant motifs.

Alil-Aga.note: Their variable adversarial encounter includes combat, capture, or negotiation.

Amelfa Timofeyevna.note: She is Dobrynya’s widowed mother and wise adviser.

Amelfa Timofeyevna.myth: Preparation for the second dragon battle
Amelfa Timofeyevna.note: She supplies Burko, the Shemakhan whip, equipment, or protective knowledge.
In some versions she helps break Marinka’s enchantment.

Andrijaš.note: The monastery inscription and early song identify Andrijaš as Marko’s brother.
Marko kills his brother during their dispute over a captured horse.

Angel of God.myth: The angel throws down the earth-weight bag
Angel of God.note: An angel supplies the bag whose weight Svyatogor cannot overcome.

Angels.myth: Ilya's withdrawal to the Kyiv caves
Angels.note: Late spiritualized texts have invisible angelic power carry Ilya to the caves.

Anna Tsarevna.note: Anna is Ivan's sister and the supernatural Raven's wife.
Ivan’s sister and Raven receive Marya and Ivan as guests.

Apraksia.note: In a Siberian variant Dobrynya rescues Apraksia instead of Zabava.

Arab king’s daughter.note: The king’s daughter frees or assists Marko during his captivity.
Arab king’s daughter.source: Marko and the Arab King’s Daughter

Arab king’s daughter.myth: Escape with the Arab king’s daughter
Arab king’s daughter.note: Marko betrays and kills his rescuer when her embrace repels or frightens him.
Arab king’s daughter.source: Marko and the Arab King’s Daughter

Baba Goryninka.note: Dobrynya fights the female warrior before Ilya enters the episode.

Baba Yaga's magic mare/foals.note: Ivan serves as herdsman to obtain the horse needed against Koschei.
Ivan wins or steals a supernatural horse capable of overtaking Koschei.

Beg Kostadin.note: Marko condemns Kostadin’s broken hospitality and mistreatment of the poor.

Black Arab.note: Marko kills the oppressor who demands bridal tribute and access to brides.

Bořivoj.note: Later genealogy regards Bořivoj as Libuše’s remote Přemyslid descendant.

Captain Leka.note: Leka hosts Marko and the other heroes seeking his sister’s hand.

Chernava.note: Sadko selects and ritually marries her but does not consummate the union.

Christian God.note: Ilya joins bogatyrs whose boast against heavenly power precedes their destruction.

Chrudoš.note: The forged poem and Smetana make Chrudoš a disputant judged by Libuše.

Churilo Plenkovich.note: They appear together as court bogatyrs without a stable exclusive adventure.

Czech.note: Lech and Czech are brothers and parallel national ancestors.
Later Czech chronicles develop Lech and Czech as related fellow migrants.
Rus and Czech are brothers and parallel ancestors without a distinct adventure.

Danilo.note: Alyosha obtains a token deceitfully and boasts of access to Danilo’s wife.

Despot Uglješa.note: Marko rejects Uglješa’s claim when judging the imperial succession.

Dmitar.note: The family inscription names Dmitar among Marko’s brothers.

Dmitry Tsarevich.note: Dmitry is Ivan's elder brother in the Firebird tale.
Dmitry participates in Ivan's murder and the theft of his prizes.

Dratewka.note: Later retellings attach Dratewka to Krak’s dragon cycle.
Dratewka.source: Kownacka’s dragon play and later retellings

Duke Momčilo.note: Epic genealogy makes Momčilo Marko’s maternal uncle and heroic predecessor.
Marko inherits or resembles the extraordinary attributes of his epic uncle.

Duke Stepanovich.note: Dobrynya leads a delegation investigating Duke’s boast of extraordinary wealth.

Dunai Ivanovich.note: Dobrynya accompanies Dunai and assists through music and courtly skill.

Eagle.note: Ivan's supernatural Eagle brother-in-law helps recover and restore him.
Eagle and his wife receive the rescued Marya and Ivan as guests.

Elena Alexandrovna.note: Volkh takes the conquered king’s wife as his own after killing Saltyk.

Elena Petrovichna.note: Alyosha courts or carries off Elena; some variants conclude with marriage.
Alyosha defeats or shames Elena’s pursuing brothers and saves her.
Alyosha boasts of sleeping with Elena, prompting her brothers to kill her.

Elena the Beautiful.myth: The Firebird and the Grey Wolf
Elena the Beautiful.note: Ivan and the abducted Elena fall in love and ultimately marry.

Elena the Beautiful.myth: The Firebird and the Grey Wolf
Elena the Beautiful.note: Ivan retains Elena after initially retrieving her for another king.

Emperor Dušan.note: Dušan is the dead sovereign whose succession and sword connect Marko to the old empire.

Emperor Uroš.note: Marko truthfully awards the disputed imperial succession to Uroš.
Uroš blesses Marko with unsurpassed future fame.

Falcon.note: Ivan's supernatural Falcon brother-in-law helps locate and restore his body.
Falcon and his wife receive the rescued Marya and Ivan as guests.

Firebird.myth: The Firebird and the Grey Wolf
Firebird.note: Ivan captures its feather and later takes the bird for his father.
Ivan captures, releases, and later summons the Firebird against Koschei.
The released Firebird gives Ivan a magic feather for summoning her.

General Vuča.note: Marko defeats Vuča’s forces while rescuing his captured companions.

God.note: After Alyosha prays, providential rain wets Tugarin’s paper wings.
God grants Marko his extraordinary strength in Bulgarian and Macedonian legends.
God removes or tests Marko’s supernatural strength in regional legends.
God preserves Marko in a cave until the people need him again.
God causes the unliftable bag to humble Svyatogor's boastful strength.

Gojko Mrnjavčević.note: Marko rejects his uncle Gojko’s claim to the succession.

Golden-maned horse.note: Ivan obtains the supernatural horse after mishandling its golden bridle.

Grey Wolf.myth: The Firebird and the Grey Wolf
Grey Wolf.note: The Wolf carries, advises, revives, and helps Ivan recover his prizes.

Idolishche.note: Alyosha and the disguised bogatyrs fight Idolishche and his forces.
Idolishche.source: Tale of the Seven Russian Bogatyrs

Idolishche Poganoe.note: Disguised as a pilgrim, Ilya kills the monstrous pagan invader.

Ilya Pechersky.note: Post-medieval devotion identifies the bylina hero with the Kyiv cave monk.

Ivan Godinovich.note: Dobrynya sometimes accompanies or is associated with Ivan’s expedition.

Ivan Kosančić.note: Marko rescues Ivan Kosančić from General Vuča.

Ivaniš.note: The family inscription names Ivaniš among Marko’s brothers.

Jevrosima.note: Epic tradition makes Jevrosima Marko’s mother.
She counsels Marko toward truth, labor, restraint, and justice.

Kalin Tsar.note: Ilya rejects Kalin's recruitment and defeats his invading forces.

Kasyan Mikhailovich.note: Alyosha plants a silver cup and falsely accuses Kasyan of theft.
Alyosha unsuccessfully attempts to procure Kasyan for Princess Apraksia.

Kazi.note: Kazi joins Libuše’s council to determine the future ruler.

King Matthias.note: Regional variants anachronistically place Marko alongside Matthias or other Hungarian rulers.

King Vukašin.note: Vukašin is Marko’s historical and nearly universal epic father.
Vukašin attacks and curses Marko for awarding the succession to Uroš.

Krak the Younger.note: Długosz names Krak the Younger as Krak’s son.
Wanda and Krak the Younger are children of Krak.

Krak’s elder son.note: Krak’s elder son helps defeat the monster before his brother murders him.

Krak’s younger son.note: Krak’s younger son helps kill the monster, murders his brother, and is exiled.

Krasava.note: In Smetana’s opera, Libuše directs Krasava’s reconciliation with Chrudoš.

Krok.note: Libuše is Krok’s youngest daughter and succeeds him as judge.

Lech.note: Długosz names Lech as Krak’s son.
Wanda and Lech are children of Krak.

Lutobor.note: Lutobor appears as an elder at Libuše’s court.

Marfa Vseslavyevna.note: She is Volkh’s mother and receives his command to arm him.

Marinka.note: The enchantress attempts to seduce or sexually dominate Dobrynya.
After his refusal, Marinka transforms him into an aurochs or another animal.

Marinka.myth: Violent conclusion of the Marinka episode
Marinka.note: In some conclusions Dobrynya kills or mutilates the defeated enchantress.

Marya Tsarevna.note: Marya is Ivan's sister and the supernatural Falcon's wife.
Ivan’s sister and Falcon receive Marya and Ivan as guests.

Meh.note: Regional Croatian tradition makes Meh a brother of Čeh and Leh.

Mikola Mozhaisky.note: He helps Sadko end the destructive performance and escape the underwater realm.
He instructs Sadko to break his strings, choose Chernava, and avoid consummation.

Milan Toplica.note: Marko rescues Milan Toplica from General Vuča.

Miloš Obilić.note: Miloš accompanies Marko and Relja as a fellow suitor.
Marko forces the vila who shot Miloš to heal him.

Miloš of Pocerje.note: Marko rescues Miloš of Pocerje from General Vuča.

Mina of Kostur.note: Marko returns in monastic disguise to recover his woman or home.
Marko takes revenge after Mina abducts or holds his woman or household.

Mother Moist Earth.note: Later interpretation calls Mikula her beloved son; early songs give no stable genealogy.
The personified earth cannot bear Svyatogor and defeats his strength through its weight.

Musa Kesedžija.note: Marko duels the extraordinarily strong outlaw Musa.
Using vila advice and a concealed weapon, Marko kills Musa and mourns him.

Nastasia Mikulishna.note: Dobrynya attacks or tests her, but she physically overmatches him.
The female warrior captures Dobrynya, selects him, and becomes his wife.

Nastasya Nikulichna.note: Alyosha attempts to marry Nastasya while her husband Dobrynya remains alive.

Nastas’ia Mikulichna.note: Northern tradition names Nastas’ia as Mikula’s daughter.

Nezamysl.note: Later genealogies explicitly make Nezamysl the son of Libuše and Přemysl.

Nightingale the Robber.note: Ilya wounds Nightingale, withstands his whistle, and takes him captive.
Ilya takes the destructive robber outside and kills him.

Nikita Kozhemyaka.note: Rou’s film replaces Ivan with Nikita Kozhemyaka as Marya’s rescuer.

Nikita Romanovich.note: Named as Dobrynya’s deceased father in some genealogical openings.

Ocean-Sea.note: He receives Sadko in his marine realm and consents to Sadko marrying Volkhova.

Old Pilgrim.myth: End of the Sea King’s power
Old Pilgrim.note: The saint-like apparition ends the marine power obstructing Sadko’s return.

Olga Tsarevna.note: Olga is Ivan's sister and the supernatural Eagle's wife.
Ivan’s sister and Eagle receive Marya and Ivan as guests.

Pagan gods.note: Wanda offers her life to the pagan gods in gratitude for victory.

Pan, prince of Pannonia.note: Pan is named as the father of Lech, Rus, and Czech.

Petrovich brothers.note: Alyosha fights or shames the brothers pursuing him and their sister.

Philip the Magyar.note: Marko defeats or humiliates the rival Philip.

Prince Vladimir.note: Vladimir grants Vol’ga three towns and their tribute revenues.

Prophet Elijah.note: Later folklore associates them through name, thunder, martial power, and feast-day culture.

Přemysl.note: Libuše foretells, summons and marries the ploughman Přemysl.
Libuše and Přemysl rule together and establish the land’s laws.
Přemysl is present when Libuše prophesies Prague’s foundation.

Queen Elena.note: Historical reconstruction identifies Elena as Marko’s mother.

Radmila.note: Radmila participates in Libuše’s court in Smetana’s opera.

Radovan.note: Radovan announces reconciliation and acclaims Libuše and Přemysl.

Raven.note: Ivan's supernatural Raven brother-in-law helps recover and restore him.
Raven and his wife receive the rescued Marya and Ivan as guests.

Raven/Raven-son.note: Under the Wolf's threat, the Raven obtains dead and living waters.

Relja Krilatica.note: Relja accompanies Marko and Miloš as a fellow hero and suitor.

Roksanda.note: After Roksanda insults the suitors, Marko mutilates and blinds her.

Rytigier.note: Wanda refuses the foreign ruler’s marriage proposal.
Rytigier invades Wanda’s realm, is defeated, and kills himself.

Saint George.note: Modern comparativists propose an analogue; no primary narrative identifies or joins them.

Saltyk Stavrulyevich.note: Volkh invades Saltyk’s city and smashes him against the palace floor.

Samson Samoilovich.note: Ilya summons the senior, godfather-like bogatyr to defend Kyiv.

Sea King.note: Pleased by Sadko’s music, he reveals how Sadko can win wealth.
He stops Sadko’s ships and demands tribute or Sadko as a living sacrifice.
Sadko is compelled to play gusli while the king’s dance wrecks ships.
The king presents hundreds of maidens and offers Sadko an otherworld bride.

Sea Tsar.note: Claimed through an inadvertent promise, Ivan must perform the Sea Tsar's tasks.

Sea Tsar.myth: Transformative flight from the Sea Tsar
Sea Tsar.note: Ivan escapes the Sea Tsar with Vasilisa's transformations and directions.

Sinbad.note: American distributors renamed Sadko as Sinbad in a recut Soviet film.

Sister of the Sun.myth: The Witch and the Sun's Sister
Sister of the Sun.note: The Sister of the Sun shelters or aids an Ivan in this tale.

Sivka-Burka.note: The magic horse becomes Ivan's helper in regional or twentieth-century composites.

Skub.note: The cobbler advises Krak how to kill the dragon.

Skub.myth: Skuba rewarded after the dragon’s death
Skub.note: Krak rewards the cobbler for devising the dragon-killing stratagem.

Slavoj.note: The opera makes Slavoj Wanda’s beloved and military champion.

Sokolnik.note: Sokolnik is Ilya's son by a foreign female warrior.
Father and son fight before tokens or testimony reveal their kinship.
In many versions Ilya kills his son after Sokolnik attacks him sleeping.
Softer variants end with father and son reconciled and Sokolnik released.

Solovei Budimirovich.note: They share court narratives, though direct interaction depends on the variant.

Sultan.note: Marko repeatedly appears as the sultan’s warrior and insolent vassal.
The sultan summons or releases Marko to defeat Musa.
Marko publicly defies the sultan’s regulation and compels tolerance of his drinking.

Svantovít.myth: Chorus invokes Svantovít in Wanda’s realm
Svantovít.note: The operatic chorus invokes Svantovít within Wanda’s pagan kingdom.

Tetka.note: Tetka joins Libuše’s council to determine the future ruler.

Thracian Horseman.note: Modern scholars hypothesize iconographic ancestry, without direct traditional identification.

Timanya.note: Timanya appears as Alyosha’s fellow champion in successive chronicle compilations.

Torop.note: Torop appears as Alyosha’s servant in chronicles and cross-influenced traditions.

Tugarin.note: Modern collective adaptations place Ilya and Tugarin in the same narratives.

Tugarin Zmeyevich.note: Alyosha fights Tugarin using disguise, diversion, horsemanship, or providential rain.
Alyosha kills and often beheads the fallen winged or serpentine enemy.
Alyosha feigns deafness, disguises himself, or tricks Tugarin into looking backward.

Twelve Arabs.note: Marko confronts and defeats the collective of twelve adversaries.

Underwater Queen.note: She explains the deadly dance and advises Sadko how to stop and choose a bride.

Unnamed Alemannic tyrant.note: The tyrant invades Wanda’s realm, but his army refuses to fight her.

Vasilisa Mikulichna.note: Northern and Kenozero genealogical tradition names Vasilisa as Mikula’s daughter.

Vasilisa the Wise.note: Later films rename or conflate the magical bride with Vasilisa the Beautiful.

Vasilisa the Wise, daughter of the Sea T.note: Ivan marries the Sea Tsar's magically capable daughter.
Vasilisa completes Ivan's impossible tasks and directs their escape.

Vasily Kazimirovich.note: Dobrynya supports Vasily with diplomacy, music, gaming, archery, and wrestling.

Vasily Tsarevich.note: Vasily is Ivan's elder brother in the Firebird tale.
Vasily helps murder Ivan and later attempts to marry Elena.

Vidosava.note: Momčilo’s treacherous wife is explicitly rejected as Marko’s mother.

Vila Ravijojla.note: Marko pursues and threatens the vila after she shoots Miloš.
Marko catches the vila and forces her to heal Miloš.

Vilina.note: Some Croatian variants add Vilina as sister of Čeh, Leh, and Meh.

Vlasta.note: Later tradition makes Vlasta Libuše’s captain, companion or attendant.

Volga Sviatoslavovich.note: Volga invites Mikula into his retinue, and they travel together.
Volga’s retinue cannot move Mikula’s plough, which Mikula lifts effortlessly.
In some variants, Mikula’s workhorse outruns Volga’s princely horse.
Mikula saves Volga and his men from hostile townspeople.
In some endings, Volga makes Mikula governor or grants him towns.

Volkhova.note: She loves Sadko and becomes his supernatural bride in the opera.
She releases Sadko from the marine realm before becoming the Volkhov River.

Wawel monster.myth: Sulphur-filled hides kill the Wawel monster
Wawel monster.note: Krak devises the baited-hide trap that kills the monster.

White Eagle.note: Lech sees the eagle and adopts it as his people’s emblem.

White Polyanin.note: Ivan fights the formidable White Polyanin in versions of their encounter.
After rivalry, Ivan befriends or cooperates with the White Polyanin.

Yan Usmoshvets.note: Alexander Popovich and Yan jointly defeat Pechenegs and capture Rodman’s family.

Yekim Ivanovich.note: Yekim travels as Alyosha’s squire and sometimes catches Tugarin’s thrown knife.

Zabava Putiatichna.note: Dobrynya frees Zabava from the dragon’s captivity.
In some versions he refuses her offer because of rank or status.

Zhidovin.myth: The foreign braggart at the outpost
Zhidovin.note: Ilya defeats the boastful foreign challenger in single combat.

Zlatogorka.note: The foreign female warrior becomes Ilya's lover or wife and bears Sokolnik.
Some variants have Ilya defeat the female warrior before courting her.

Zmei Gorynych.myth: First encounter at the Puchai River
Zmei Gorynych.note: Unarmed Dobrynya defeats the serpent using the heavy Greek cap.

Zmei Gorynych.myth: Pact after the first dragon battle
Zmei Gorynych.note: Dobrynya grants mercy and agrees to mutual nonaggression with the serpent.
After the serpent breaks their pact, Dobrynya fights and kills it.
Popular retellings identify Volkh’s unnamed serpent father as Zmei Gorynych.

Zmey Gorynych.note: Ivan fights Zmey Gorynych in various later tales, plays, and adaptations.

the Seven Bogatyrs.note: Alyosha joins their disguised expedition and battle against numerous enemies.
the Seven Bogatyrs.source: Tale of the Seven Russian Bogatyrs

the forty kaliki.note: Alyosha insults and searches the pilgrims but fails through discourtesy.

unnamed vila foster-mother.note: Some regional traditions make an unnamed vila Marko’s supernatural mother.
A vila suckles the abandoned Marko and becomes his foster-mother.
A vila rewards Marko with milk that confers supernatural strength.
In some songs a vila acts as Marko’s supernatural adviser.

Đemo the Mountaineer.note: After Đemo captures or threatens him, Marko escapes and defeats him.

Świętowit.myth: Pagan invocations by the three founders
Świętowit.note: Some modern stories have the founders invoke Świętowit, unlike medieval accounts.

Šarac.note: Marko’s extraordinary horse serves as his trusted companion in numerous adventures.
Marko kills Šarac so that no Turk can ride him.

Šťáhlav.note: The forged poem and Smetana make Šťáhlav the other disputant Libuše judges.
